prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the molecular basis of glue degraders

statement.case_for: I have moved from my round-1 pairing of B055 and B006 to B029 as a single part. The decisive point is that the round-1 exchange tested my own scientific criteria and my pairing did not hold up under them. My case for B055 rested on physical-chemical substance, yet four colleagues independently pressed the same weakness: which cellular assemblies are genuinely phase-separated, and which are functionally driven by it, remains disputed, and the credit sits among five people with a three-person cap. I raised exactly those caveats in my own case_against, so I cannot ask the committee to discount them. B029 has none of that problem at the level of mechanism. Induced proximity through ternary-complex formation, E3 ligase recruitment, and cereblon as the thalidomide target are settled, structurally characterised and independently reproduced over two decades. The chemical principle is new: occupancy-driven inhibition is replaced by event-driven, catalytic removal, and the design variables (linker, ligase ligand, cooperativity) are chemical. For the third name I choose Handa over Ciulli because the citation should cover both the PROTAC strand and the glue strand, and Handa's identification of cereblon is the discovery that explains an old drug and made rational glue design possible. Crews and Deshaies are common to every B029 configuration in the room.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet approved, so the therapeutic vindication is prospective, and a committee that waits for clinical confirmation could reasonably defer. Attribution is crowded: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto (co-author of the 2001 paper), Ito, Gray and Kim all have credible claims that the three-name cap excludes. PROTACs and molecular glues arose as separate lineages, and one citation risks blurring two histories, although I judge that a prize naming only the heterobifunctional strand would read as the more incomplete choice. My move also gives up a two-part prize with a plain citation each; with B029 needing all three names, no second part is possible, and I accept that cost. B055 and B006 remain, in my view, real achievements that I do not think this committee has judged unfairly, but I cannot defend them as stronger than B029 on maturity or support.

responses.point: A degrader is a molecule with a demonstrated effect that can be tested directly, whereas the condensate framework risks locking in a contested reading; and the citation should be limited to heterobifunctional PROTACs with Ciulli as the third name.
responses.response: I accept your first point and it is the main reason I have moved: the dispute over how many cellular assemblies are truly phase-separated is one I flagged myself, and a prize should not rest on it. I part from you on scope. A PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli leaves out the cereblon mechanism that explains thalidomide-class drugs and led to rational glue design, and I would not want the prize to read as if that strand were a footnote. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are important design contributions, but I weigh the discovery of the molecular target of an old drug as the more distinct step, so I name Handa.

responses.point: Moving from a trio with Ciulli to Crews, Deshaies and Handa lets one prize honour both the PROTAC and glue strands, and the chair notes that crediting five people for condensates is crowded.
responses.response: I follow the same reasoning and reach the same trio. You also name the real cost, that pairing two lineages can dilute the citation, and I think the wording matters: it should say that small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system, then name PROTACs and the molecular basis of glues as the two routes, rather than claim one invention. I also agree with your point that attribution among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is harder than I presented it, and that is part of why B055 is now my first alternative rather than my preferred part.

responses.point: Aili argues that mechanistic confirmation and field adoption matter more than regulatory approval, and that the cereblon and PROTAC strands together make B029 the most chemically original of the leading candidates; Aili also noted that waiting for the field to settle was my own reasoning against B055.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of maturity. The absence of an approved degrader is a real caution, but the chemistry does not depend on it: ternary complexes are crystallographically defined, and many groups reproduce degradation, so the principle is established whatever the regulatory outcome. Since this is the candidate nearest to your research on peptide self-assembly and you still rank it first, I take that as a mark in its favour, not a bias. Your point that I would rather wait for condensates to settle is fair, and I apply the same standard to B029 and find it met. I do share your worry that a combined PROTAC and glue citation may be criticised as merging two discoveries.

responses.point: Brzezinski concedes that B056 is the cleanest mechanistic science but has no support beyond his own ballot, and moved to B029 because a prize configuration has to survive discussion; he also treats Ciulli as a live contender over Deshaies.
responses.response: I respect that move and it parallels mine: preferring something on scientific taste is different from being able to defend it against the room. On Ciulli versus Deshaies, I do not think Deshaies should be displaced. Deshaies co-authored the 2001 PROTAC proof of principle with Crews, and removing a founder of the concept to make room for later design work would be harder to justify than leaving Ciulli out, although I recognise that this exclusion is a real cost. I would have no objection to a lower-profile mention of Ciulli's structural work in the prize background material.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that B029 survives every lens in the room and that keeping Handa makes the prize about the principle, not one compound class.
responses.response: I agree, and the chair's observation that six of eight round-1 positions already lie with B029 supports that. I would add that the physical-chemical angle favours it too: induced proximity is an effective-molarity and cooperativity argument that can be measured and tuned, which is a firmer basis than the in vivo phase-diagram arguments I had relied on. I also note your caution that crediting Handa should not imply that Sakamoto, Gray and Ito were overlooked, and I would want the citation text to avoid any claim of sole priority.

uncertainties: Whether the committee should defer B029 until at least one degrader drug is approved, and what evidence it would treat as sufficient; I judge the mechanism to be established but cannot resolve the clinical question.

Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I weigh target identification of cereblon more heavily than VHL-ligand design, but I recognise the difference is one of judgement and the opening ballots split.
Whether one citation can cover PROTACs and glue degraders without misstating the two histories, and whether Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are unfairly left out.

Whether biomolecular condensates (B055) will in time be judged a settled chemistry achievement, and whether Cullis alone is a fair reading of the lipid nanoparticle lineage in B006; both remain my alternatives.
statement.conflict_note: My scientific work on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly is close to B055 and B006, which were in my round-1 configuration and are now my alternatives; I have no tie to any credited name on any shortlisted part. B029 is outside my own research field, so I have no field-based stake in it. I share Lund University with Linke and Somfai and have field overlap with Aili and Brzezinski, none of which requires recusal. My earlier disclosure stands and no recusal is needed.
